posts.caption:
In addition to acting, not so long ago, I lived life as a jeweler. I like to say I’m on sabbatical, still some 10+ years later.
Back in 2006, Wes asked me to make a brooch for the Chief Steward’s uniform. Our base for the film was in Jodhpur and my workshop wasn’t too, too far away in Jaipur.
My work has always taken inspiration from the natural world, so an elephant felt fitting.
As a little side note, we later released the brooch through Yoox in support of Elephant Family. It was our first project with Elephant Family, and the beginning of what has become decades of supporting conservation.
The original brooch is now on view at the @designmuseum as part of the Wes Anderson: The Archives exhibition.
I’m not sure who made the collage in the last slide, but I’ve always loved it. Thank you to whoever did.

posts.title: “In the middle of winter I at last discovered that there was in me an invincible summer” Albert Camu
posts.caption:
“In the middle of winter I at last discovered that there was in me an invincible summer” Albert Camus

It was a long winter. At times, seemingly endless. Right as it began, my mother fell. A broken hip, surgery, then 2 1/2 months in rehab. Almost every day I drove out to Jersey to see her. On the days I couldn’t, @phasesofmoon went. 

The sandwich generation, they call us. Caught between caring for a parent and raising a child. A strange place to stand- holding both ends of time.

It was hard seeing her like that. In pain. Still. Dependent. This is the woman who made everything possible for me. And then suddenly, time, doing what time does.

As an only child, with one parent left standing, so to speak, I didn’t handle it well. Long drives in silence. The FDR feeling longer and bumpier each day. Not wanting to talk. Not wanting comfort. Not even wanting understanding. Just sitting with the grief. Forgetting to breathe properly. Wanting to be alone inside it.
Sure, a little dramatic, maybe.

I haven’t posted much since. It all felt like noise. Ocean’s favorite question right now is “What noise?” With every little creak, every passing siren, every quiet hum that most of us forget to hear. She asks it with wonder.

What noise, indeed, my love. 

It’s not in my nature to overshare on social media, but somewhere in all of this, being personal felt like the only way back in. The work is still there. The travel, the shoots, the beautiful distractions.
But sharing only the glitz started to feel insincere. After all, grief is not only integral to the human condition—it’s deeply part of the creative process.

Time has always been on my mind. In my work, in my writing. It feels less like a concept, more like a presence. Is it my collaborator—or my adversary?

Mom is home now. Moving slowly, with her walker. In good spirits. Determined.

“In the middle of winter I at last discovered that there was in me an invincible summer.” This time, that summer was my family. My dream girls @phasesofmoon and Ocean. Our extended family- you know who you are. You held me up, quietly, in all the ways that matter—even when I didn’t want it. Thank you. It was your support that got us through.

posts.title: I love this photo of me and my dad.
posts.caption:
I love this photo of me and my dad.

The weird silver lining of his premature death at 68 is that it triggered what my kids call my recent “glow up” a.k.a. getting my own health in order. As you can see, I’m his carbon copy.

When he died of a stroke a few years ago, I was pre-diabetic and about to be declared Type II, my blood pressure was through the roof (even on meds) and my cholesterol was completely out of whack…to name just a few of the biggies on a long list. Earlier this week, I had my annual physical: A1c is normal, blood pressure so low that I was getting light-headed so he pulled me down to the lowest BP dose, and he’s recommending I get a heart scan because he thinks I’m a good candidate for being pulled off of statins since my LDL is now so low.

Happy Father’s Day! You are loved!

I think we all need to learn to just be ourselves a little more.

There’s already so much going on in the world. So many complications, news,so many things to complain about, so many things we can’t control.

And somewhere in all of this, maybe we forget that we’re actually here to live.
Like… we know how this ends, right? We all have the same truth waiting for us at the end of the day death. Sounds a little rude to say it like that, but it’s true.
So maybe, while we’re here, we can try to make this life a little lighter.

Sort your fights before you go to sleep. Say what you feel. Forgive a little, laugh. Let go of things that don’t deserve so much space in your head.

And wake up the next morning with a completely new feeling.
Maybe nothing around you has changed.

But you have.

posts.title: In 2018 I met with an accident on the set of a tv show that I was doing. Till date I get Dms why I l
posts.caption:
In 2018 I met with an accident on the set of a tv show that I was doing. Till date I get Dms why I left that show abruptly and why I never made it back on the show. So today I decided to share this story with all of you. I was shooting with a dog and it happened to bite me right under my eye. I still get flashes of that incident it was bizarre. I wasn’t used to seeing my face like that I was losing a lot of work because of that. The same year, before my wound could heal completely, I also lost my father within a month of that incident. Losing my father was a deeper scar than the one I had on my face. And to top it up, while I still hadn’t recovered from the pain of losing him my personal life also started falling apart . I started to feel that I am going to lose everything.. I started feeling scared, insecure and anxious that I will lose my mom,my family I was literally living in fear coz everything was just being taken away from me… I was only left with my trauma. 

•Why I’m sharing it today?? Coz I feel an actor is misunderstood so easily and people think all actors are privileged. But we are also normal human beings and as humans we also experience all kinds of hardships and we still keep our mouth shut and most of the time don’t share our sad stories openly coz even after all the s**t we experience, we still have to show up like soldiers. We still have to fight our battles silently. We still have to give our flesh and blood to our work. We still have to be loyal to a profession which is so ruthless. We still have to entertain you, make y’all laugh. 
•I was running away from my pain for a couple years and not fully accepting what was happening to me but eventually I had to. Once I accepted the reality I used my pain as the fire in me. I worked hard on myself to come out of darkness. Life of an artist is uncertain… We are mad people! And that’s the beauty of living for art. It can numb the pain at least if it can’t save you!!! I hope together we can make this world a kinder place to coexist and learn from each other’s lives!
P.s I still love dogs 🐕 ❤️

There’s something strange about evenings.

As the light begins to fade,
the world gets quieter…
but somehow, the mind gets louder.

One thought becomes another.
A memory turns into a possibility.
A conversation that never happened suddenly feels real.
A place you’ve never been to…
a life you never lived…
a moment that exists only in your imagination.

And before you know it,
you’ve travelled through a hundred places,
lived a hundred moments,
felt a hundred emotions…

without ever leaving the chair.

It’s almost funny,
how the mind can make you feel like you’ve lived an entire lifetime
while your body has been sitting in the exact same place.

And then the evening ends.

You look around.

Nothing happened.

No one came.
No journey was taken.
No conversation actually happened.

It was all just you…

and the thousand lives your mind created
while you were sitting still.…

posts.title: Manto saab, mere dost.
posts.caption:
Manto saab, mere dost. 

18 January. This day, you left the world. It’s been 67 years, but I wish to tell you that you live in the hearts of many. You’ve left a treasure for people who find you in your afsanay, afsanche, mazmoons, khats and qisses. It’s been 4 years to our friendship, Manto saab. A long long time ago, we met at Dilli’s Big Book Bazaar and see, we have come so far. 

Look, I see a reflection of you in me, Manto saab. Is that Kurta the right way? The spectacles too. Sorry couldn’t get Cavanders, and you know I don’t smoke. I’m just posing. Also, I’m on a hunt to find that specific bottle of alcohol. I’m sure about the jutti though. But before we go on stage together this year, I know all of it will align. 

I managed to get a watch from Nanu’s collection, which is from the time of partition. Who knows it better than you about the time that shook people, scattered families, disheartened many, left a void. That notebook of mine is full of our conversations. It’s one sided but I know what you’ll reply. 

I will visit Bombay soon too. I can’t wait to see where you lived. Adelphi Chambers, Clare Road, Byculla, Sarvi. I wish to visit that before we do a theatrical play in Dilli. ‘Hum jeb katre hain Manto saab, jo apni jeb khud kaat te hain, aur ek kahani nikal ke bahar aajati hai.’

We share so much. The love for storytelling, the passion of clicking photographs. A story awaits for this world. Ye kahani humare naam. Bohot jald. Now that you’ve made me wear white too. I think it will be heart-warming for this world to witness our sensitivities. Aao, 2023 main afsaane bunte hain. :’)

Manto, Mere Dost. Premiere Show.
Delhi. 

It took me 7 years to make this show. It took my heart, my soul, my patience. It broke me, it left me into peaces, it disturbed me, it chose me, it was meant to happen through me.

Kya yeh naatak karna zaroori hai? 
Haan, iska mere zehen se nikalna bohot zaroori hai. 
Par yahi kahani kyun? 
Kuch kahaniyan aap khud likhte hain, lekin iss kahani ne mujhe chuna hai.

14 August 2026 has become historic for me. To everyone who came and became a part of this beautiful evening, I’m grateful. 

To the ones who stole the posters of the show, I must tell you, you’ll be lucky in times to come, to the one person who sold the ticket in black, makes me feel, it’s going somewhere. 

When I was on stage, I could feel Manto with me, his presence surrounded me. I was in awe of what we had created, from the set to the tickets, to the lights, to the story, and the matchboxes. 

The wait won’t be long, as Manan and Manto will return back to Dilli soon and then fly to Bombay, soonest. 

Main chalta firta Bombay hoon 
- Manto
Aur, Main chalta firta Dilli hoon.
- Manan 

All my love,
Manan

posts.title: MAKING OF MANTO, MERE DOST.
posts.caption:
MAKING OF MANTO, MERE DOST. 

In a quaint little shop in Gurgaon’s Sadar Bazaar sits Jawaharlal, son of Prabhati Ram, a shoemaker who has been making leather shoes all his life. It is my honour to have met Mr. Jawahar, fondly called Babaji, who is continuing his father’s legacy.

I enter the shop. He asks me if I’m from somewhere outside. I tell him I’m from the same mohalla where his shop is, Jacob Pura. He keeps speaking names, thinking one of them would be my grandfather. Then he understands where my home is. He asks me what I want.

I scream with excitement, “A jutti. A Punjabi jutti.” Manto saab was fond of shoes, and very precise about his jutti. I don’t know how I stumbled upon this dukaan, which has been standing strong since undivided India, where I would meet a happy man, Babaji, who would craft the juttis for my theatrical show, Manto, Mere Dost.

The shop’s vintage grandeur resides in the recommendation letters put up on the walls, received by him and his father from a Major General, a District Magistrate, a Britisher, and people who wrote to them in Urdu from the other side of the border.

Their shoes have made a place in people’s lives, hearts, and homes, and their handmade jutti will be the highlight of the show.

After today, I believe I’m made for this. The universe is bringing me closer to myself, and I will revolutionise the theatrics of modern India.

This premiere show will be most special to me. I hope to see all of you there, for history, as this will be one for the ages.

posts.title: De entre todos los regalos que podías haberme hecho y me harás jamás, me quedo con el que el cielo n
posts.caption:
De entre todos los regalos que podías haberme hecho y me harás jamás, me quedo con el que el cielo nos bajó por sorpresa a los dos.

Sobre el mar, puro como un folio en blanco, caminaba la luz de la mañana recién estrenada. 

Me hiciste señas para que me girase hacia el paseo. Las villas con las que tanto soñamos despiertos eran nuestras en un reflejo tan delicado y a la vez tan firme que parecía duplicar una realidad que por el momento sólo está en nuestro deseo. 

Tras ellas, la montaña. Majestuosa. Una perfecta amalgama complementaria de ese rojo tan peculiar de su tierra y el verde penetrante de los pinos que bordan en las laderas aromas de vida por florecer.

Cuando volví la vista para mirarte ya no estabas. Habías avanzado hacia ese espacio en el que el infinito parece abarcable. Ese lugar que ya no es sitio, ese pequeño gran mundo donde todo lo que hay por delante es horizonte. 

Me quedé mirando tu perfil y lamenté no tener un clic a mano para guardar esa imagen en un carrete.

Y aquí me tienes, intentando encender la luz roja en el cuarto oscuro de la memoria después de enfocar con la lente del corazón. Positivando un momento que, pasados unos días, empiezo a dudar de que pasara. ¿Acaso puede el mundo que conocemos ser tan perfecto?

Y procuro exponer con delicadeza la película de ese instante en el que la silueta de las gaviotas se recortaba sobre un par de rocas que se escapaban del espigón. 

Guardo la intensidad del sol deslizándose en ligerísimas ondas sobre el agua transparente. 

Buceo en el contraste de la Torre Colomera, restos de una historia de ataques berberiscos, sobre la ligereza de un cielo profundamente azul, defensa incólume del futuro que se asoma al recuerdo de este momento en el que llegué a creerme inmortal.

Te abrazo. Ya no sé si este sabor a sal son restos de mar o es la certeza de que se puede llorar de belleza.

posts.caption:
Han pasado tres años, dos gemelos y una depresión desde estas fotos. 

No sé bien de dónde saqué las fuerzas para hacer esta boda. Bueno, sí. Del Jefe. 

Pero vamos, que dos días antes estaba desvelada con la banda sonora de un coro de voces sordas que me decían que no iba a poder. Que no sabía. Que no. No, no, no. 

Y me metía en el mar y quería que las olas me llevasen y al mismo tiempo era incapaz de dejarme mecer por la quietud y el tsunami que llevaba dentro me ahogaba y no hallaba salvavidas aunque supiera que no era necesario porque hacía pie pero en realidad era como si me hundiera en mi propia mente movediza. 

Nadie sabe lo que es ponerse detrás de una cámara y delante de ciento y pico personas cuando sólo quieres desaparecer. Cuando no soportas que te hablen, que te miren, que te sientan, que te nada. Cuando no te soportas. 

Pero hoy miro atrás, veo todo esto y pienso que lo hice bien. 

El reportaje y el puñetazo en la mesa donde parecía estar servida mi alma en pedazos. 

La clave fue ponerme en el centro. 

Y hoy, de nuevo, es el reto. Recuperada mi mente, es mi cuerpo el que reclama mi atención. Nada que no pueda solucionarse con un poquito de amor. Propio. 

P. D.: Muchas felicidades, María y Carlos. Qué alegría haber podido escribir esa primera página de vuestro libro de recuerdos familiar.

posts.caption:

Pensé que hacer fotos para el libro de @ignacioguio (@mrediciones ), uno de los referentes de jardinería en redes sociales, me redimiría. Como si los cuidados para la vida –aunque sea la vida vegetal– pudiesen aprenderse en una mañana y sólo por proximidad. 

Pero una no puede dar nada por supuesto. Ni siquiera sus escasas dotes para la jardinería. Porque hete aquí que, desde que hicimos la reforma en casa, no sé si el ambiente se ha reformado también, pero el caso es que mis amigas verdes están de lo más lustrosas.

Por eso me extrañó sobremanera que la flor globo que mi madre me regaló para mi último cumpleaños no durase ni dos telediarios. Lo achaqué a la ola de calor. La puse a la sombra. La regué –lo justo–. La refresqué con flus flus. Le corté los tallos secos. Le hablé bonito.

posts.title: Si sigo así no sigo.
posts.caption:
Si sigo así no sigo.
Llevo tiempo preguntándome cómo es que trabajo cada vez más horas y la cuenta corriente se hace cada vez más pequeña.

No tengo huecos libres que llevarme a la agenda y, en lugar de prosperar, mis ahorros están desapareciendo.
Primero lo achaqué a la reforma de nuestra casa. A la boda, también.
Luego, a algún que otro capricho.
Sobre todo, a haberme acostumbrado a sobrevivir, a ir a salto de mata y no pararme a cuidar de mí ni de mis finanzas.

Ayer saqué un rato para tirar de calculadora.
Y sabía que los tiros iban por ahí –estoy desinformada, pero no tanto–. Sólo que no pensaba que fuera para tanto.

Desde 2022, algunos de los costes fijos de mi negocio se han incrementado hasta en más del 100%:
📷 Tarjetas de memoria: + 120% (cada año renuevo al menos 4).
💾 Discos duros: + 55% (cada año lleno una media de 3).
💻 Programas de edición: + 30% (imprescindibles para mis reportajes).
📓 Álbumes: + 20% (sí, sigo entregando papel).
📈 Cuota de autónomos: + 12% (en fin…).
🧮 Gestoría: + 10% (podría llevarme yo las cuentas, pero no tendría paz mental para dedicársela a mis clientes).

Desde 2022, mis tarifas no han variado.

Y ya es insostenible.

A partir de septiembre actualizaré mis precios. Lo justo para seguir manteniendo la calidad y la excelencia que siempre he ofrecido y a la que no pienso renunciar. Porque si es el precio de seguir, no seguiré pagándolo.

Si estabas pensando en disfrutar de alguno de mis reportajes, puedes contratarlos durante julio y agosto al mismo precio de 2022 (me da vergüenza hasta escribirlo).

Y si no, tranquilidad: te voy a querer igual y me encantará seguirte viendo por aquí.

posts.caption:
Stopped by Brewyard Specialty Coffee on Law College Road for what I thought would be a quick cup of coffee.

Instead, I ended up spending the next few minutes trying to figure out how a coffee could taste so different from anything I’ve had before.

This V60 was brewed using Harley Estate’s Nitrogen Maceration lot from Manjarabad. The aroma was intensely fruity, reminding me of ripe cherries and raisins, with a sweet wine-like character that immediately stood out. As the coffee cooled, layers of dark fruits and cashew apple became more noticeable, making every sip slightly different from the last.

The nitrogen maceration process adds a unique depth and complexity to the cup, creating a coffee that’s juicy, vibrant, and packed with character while still maintaining a clean finish.

One of the things I love about specialty coffee is that every cup tells a different story. This one started in the hills of Karnataka and somehow found its way into my hands at a beautiful café in Pune.

Definitely one of the most memorable pour-overs I’ve had recently.

posts.caption:
Harley Estate sits deep in Karnataka, in the rolling hills of Sakleshpur. Established in 1864, Harley has a rich heritage of growing robusta and arabica, but also peppercorn, areca, cardamom, and cocoa.

Darkwoods has been working with Harley Estate from our early beginnings. Their signature specialty washed robusta is a vital part of our espresso blends (Deer Hill and Black Hill), giving the coffee a beautifully complex depth and sweetness, and excellent crema.

Leon and Damian visited Harley in January, ahead of a busy harvest, and everything was running like a well-oiled machine. Purnesh oversees the day-to-day operations, while his daughters, Tapaswini and Chandini, lead the marketing and the domestic coffee scene with their own brand, ‘Classic’.

Arriving at Harley, they saw the first crop of sundried arabicas spread out in the warm afternoon sun, remarkably neat and uniform. The patios meticulously maintained, and the attention to detail second to none.

The farm is now well over 800 acres after acquiring the neighbouring Raxidi Estate, yet it still feels intimate and charming, with beautiful backdrops and dense, lush forests woven between the coffee lots. Harley Estate truly is one of a kind.
We were welcomed with incredible hospitality, kindness, and enthusiasm by the entire team, and were even lucky enough to spot a wild Monsoon Hornbill while cupping some delicious coffees.

These memories and moments are why people like Purnesh, and places like @harleyestate, will always hold a special place in our coffee journey.

posts.title: "I think I became a writer because I used to write letters to my friends, and I used to love writing
posts.caption:
"I think I became a writer because I used to write letters to my friends, and I used to love writing them. I loved the idea that you can put marks on a page and send it off, and two days later, someone laughs somewhere else in the world."
~David Nicholls
.
"I love the rebelliousness of snail mail, and I love anything that can arrive with a postage stamp. There's something about that person's breath and hands on the letter."
~Diane Lane
.
My love for writing and reading started off around the same time. One of the very first books I've ever read in my life (or remember of), is this one. 'Love from your friend, Hannah'

This book is written in the form of letters written by Hannah to her grandparents, Aunt, the President of USA, and all in search of a right pen pal for her. She eventually does find a wonderful friend who talks of various things under the sun. The childhood innocence mixed with the joy of experiencing Hannah's life through her beautiful letters.

It all starts when her best friend Agnes, who was also her neighbour moves and promises to remain her pen-pal. Hannah writes many lettersto her, and receives no answer in return. And one can imagine the frustration of the same, having experienced many such moments in our modern life as well.

When I come to think of it, I was quite a kid at 12 to look for pen-pals across the globe to write to. But when I look back, it was worth the joy.

More than just writing, I started craving for writing letters, and making new pen-pals. The joy of receiving letters, and even better, writing them is unmatched. If you've ever received a letter from me, EVER, be sure you've meant a lot to me at some point in time. There's no way denying that.

Recently when I started looking for this book, it wasn't available in India. My lovely friend bought it for me in the US, and sent it across to me. Also, a box, a precious one to make home for all my letters. She knows how much letters mean to me! ✉

If you've ever wanted to travel back in time, I'd highly recommend writing a letter or two. I keep procrastinating this, but finally hoping to write regularly. Please do feel free to ask for a postcard from me. (DM me your address)

posts.title: ▶️ If money wasn’t a limitation, what would you change about your life?
posts.caption:
▶️ If money wasn’t a limitation, what would you change about your life?

I wanted to read something different, and that’s when I picked up Blessed Be the Billionaires. What intrigued me was the question at the heart of the book: What if it were illegal to be rich? What happens when extreme wealth becomes a crime? And can capitalism itself be changed?

Blessed Be the Billionaires by Luc Upson explores these questions through a compelling story set in the near future, where oligarchs have consolidated so much wealth that they control much of society, while the rest survive by renting from them. In this world, owning a home has become almost impossible, wealth determines power, and the gap between those who have everything and those who have almost nothing has become the new normal.

Against this backdrop, we meet Sadie, Garrett and Nishanthi – three very different people who, in their own ways, decide not to simply accept the world as it is. Sadie, Garrett and Nishanthi find themselves thrown together in an Amsterdam prison, where the larger debate over wealth suddenly becomes deeply personal. Each of them arrives with their own choices, their own reasons and their own version of what has happened.  What initially seem like three separate stories slowly begin to connect, and that’s when they begin trying to put together the pieces of the puzzle they have messed up along the way.

What I particularly enjoyed about the plot is the way Luc introduces us to the three protagonists individually before bringing them together.

posts.title: ▶️ What’s a dream you’re still chasing?
posts.caption:
▶️ What’s a dream you’re still chasing?

I literally ran to my grandmas – my dadi and nani and started asking them about their hardships and their stories as I finished reading this book. And that’s when I realised how many things we have today that make life easier for us, and how difficult it would have been for women of their time to simply survive, make choices, and still bloom so beautifully. The book also made me think about how easily we look at the women of previous generations only through the roles they played, as mothers, wives, grandmothers or homemakers, without knowing the dreams they had before those roles became such a big part of their lives. These stories make you wonder how many such stories exist within our own families that we have never stopped to ask about.

I wanted to read something that is inspiring, light, and meaningful, and that’s when I picked up this book. Right from its quirky title and cover, I knew this book would be another interesting journey, and it definitely was. Bullet Nani and Other Badass Indian Grandmas by Jasreen Mayal Khanna is a journey of 12 inspiring grandmothers who took the reins of their lives into their own hands and decided to live life on their own terms. Every grandmother you meet here has an remarkable story to tell, taking us through the ups and downs they faced at a time when girls and women were often expected to remain within the four walls of their homes. These grandmas stepped beyond those boundaries and stepped out into the world to live their dreams.

posts.caption:
▶️ what is one thing you would choose differently today?

I finished reading I Am Diya by Sangeeta Kampani, and one thought that really stayed with me was how often a woman has to fight her first battle at home before she can step out and fight the world. Diya’s journey beautifully captures this struggle of standing up for yourself, making choices that others may not understand, and eventually taking charge of your own life. At its heart, this is also a book about finding your own home within yourself. We have to build a life that feels honest and whole, no matter what it takes and no matter where life takes us. 

The story follows Diya, a woman who gets married at a young age, only to realise that her marriage is not the life she had imagined. The relationship begins to fall apart, and eventually, the situation becomes too much for her to handle.

The plot of the story is interesting and engaging, particularly because it follows Diya through different stages of her life rather than limiting itself to her marriage. Sangeeta Kampani’s writing style is direct yet poetic, with simple prose that occasionally becomes lyrical through her observations and descriptions, adding an emotional layer to the narrative.

posts.title: One of the most misunderstood concepts in the Law of Evidence is the difference between Burden of Pr
posts.caption:
One of the most misunderstood concepts in the Law of Evidence is the difference between Burden of Proof and Onus of Proof.

Many students, and even people observing court proceedings, often say “Burden of proof shift ho gaya.” But legally, that’s not correct.

The Burden of Proof generally remains on the party who is legally required to prove the case, whereas the Onus of Proof can shift from one party to another during different stages of the trial depending on the evidence produced.

Understanding this single distinction can make your concepts of the Indian Evidence Act much stronger and help you approach criminal law with greater clarity.

Save this reel for your Evidence Act revision and share it with a law student who often gets confused between these two concepts.

posts.caption:
The Secret Eligibles of Mumbai by @anmolmalik5 

What an entertaining read!!!!!
Never a dull moment here. It reads like a nice masala Bollywood romcom but somewhere the characters feels more lived in and relatable. And so many millennial coded Bombay references that i absolutely LOVE💖

If you are craving a nice Bollywood love story but something that suits the day and age we live in, then definitely give this one a shot.

Taking accountability for your actions is sexy. Communication is desirable. It takes all these entertaining elements of a good Bollywood romcom of the 2000s that we miss so much these days and blends it with 2026 awareness.

Dharam and Aran both are swoon worthy in their own right. Kim and Andie feel so relatable. Each character is so distinct than the other - it’s like there’s something for everyone. The main thing is inspite of the wealthy rich backdrop of some or most characters they feel more real and normal. Their battles seem identifiable and something you will resonate with. Empathising with them, rooting for them.

The writing is smooth, entertaining, and the pacing is consistent throughout. The climax toh won’t leave you distracted even for a second. Even if you crack it or not you will still enjoy the thrill of it!

My favourite July read and a desi romcom I enjoyed after a long time. Thank you so much @harpercollinsin for this copy!

posts.caption:
𝕭𝖔𝖔𝖐 𝕽𝖊𝖛𝖎𝖊𝖜: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Book Name: The Secret Eligibles of Mumbai
Author Name: Anmol Malik

I don't know how to start this review but WHAT A WELL WRITTEN CHAOTIC DESI ROMANCE THIS WAS!!?? 

I still need to process how can someone write a book this witty, I mean all the dramatic scenes, Kim's monologues (top tier!!) and the filmy references? A. T. E. 

Being completely honest, this book took me by surprise because I did not expect to feel all these emotions. I was laughing, sad, angry at the characters (specifically Dharam) and at the same time going "aww that is so cute". I could relate with Kim so much at so many points because of the elder sister thing and my heart broke at so many points seeing her make peace with the life she had. And that is why when Dharam came in the picture and made her smile, I was like "YASSS" but that happiness did not last long because, well I'm not going to spoil it for you. 

Andie and Aran's story left me shocked if I want to sum it up. But what a gentleman Aran is 🤌

I did not find one thing I did not like in this book because the author delivered, with everything. Banter? Check ✔️. Drama? Check ✔️. Full bollywood desi rom-com chaos?? One hundred percent check ✔️ 

A very small thing that I would have loved if it was there was if we got a little more of Kim and Dharam's after getting into relationship moments. 

Regardless, this book has everything to qualify for a movie adaptation so I am praying and manifesting it gets picked up 🤞. 

If you are in a mood of a feel good , desi romance with A LOT of drama and chaos, this is for you!! 

P. S. I am a homcha fan too 👀🤭 (ifykyk)
